answer: Every key cut in the town is registered with the guild, and the bitting code of each key is written in the guild book. A pearl key cut by an unlicensed smith fails the code: at the hollow of the cuts the depths must match the registered pattern, and a strange key cuts differently. Forging a key means bribing a locksmith, cutting a hundred trial keys and paying 9,100, and the atlas book is read at every door, so a key whose code belongs to no lock is snapped.
